text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said Microsoft founder Bill Gates has agreed to be a member of an advisory board which is developing Malaysia's high-technology area, Multimedia Super Corridor.

- Information chief of Mahathir's UMNO party, Mohamad Yusof Nor urged the government to take stern action acting human rights groups which plan to hold a public meeting to discuss alleged police abuses.

- Malayan United Industries, which has turned loss-making diversified firm Pengkalen Holdings Bhd back into shape in four months, says there is much potential to tap from within the group, said MUI chief operating officer Chong Kee Hong.

- Eldest son of Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik and new major shareholder of Berjaya Industrial Bhd, Ling Hee Leong, said he wants the company to be his listed flagship. Among new businesses planned are strategic investments, financial services and property development.

- DCB Sakura Merchant Bankers Bhd chairman Abdul Rashid Hussain said the firm will continue to focus on merchant banking and not overlap its activities with other related institutions within the DCB Holdings Bhd and Rashid Hussain Bhd family.
